title: Apollo — Variants across tellings
summary: Apollo is god of the sun, music, prophecy, and healing. This study compares how different sources tell the tale.
body:
Apollo is god of the sun, music, prophecy, and healing. His oracle at Delphi was consulted by kings and city-states.

No myth has one true version. Apollo survives in competing tellings — poets, priests, and painters each shaping it to their purpose. The variants disagree, and the disagreements are themselves revealing. Viewed through a narrative lens, Apollo is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

The 'real' Apollo is the whole cloud of versions, not any single text. A fourth sub-question examines the moral the myth was meant to teach its first hearers. Related entries in this archive: Minotaur and Ziggurats.
